title: Choose the visual world for ccdesk
question: The roll assigned the Swiss rail timetable. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Timetable & Line Map
options.lineage: Swiss rail timetables and route strip maps
options.thesis: Every directory is a line: config loads stop by stop, and every value carries the line bullet of the file it came from.
materials: route bullets G P L M
options.viewport: Left rail of directories; across the top, the current repo's route strip (Global → parent → Project → Local → Memory) with counts at each stop; below, a timetable-ruled table of everything loaded here; right, the raw file with its path.
options.risk: Line colours must stay legible for colour-blind users (you use dark-daltonized), so every colour also carries a letter bullet.

raised.raise: Every key, path and count sits in tabular monospace columns, aligned to the character.
One strict row grid: every row in every table has the same height, so the page reflows by whole rows.
Settings compare view registers User, Project, Local and Managed as aligned columns on one baseline.
The route strip and the list are one space: click a stop to jump to its rows, select a row to light its stop.
Line colours stay flat and unmodulated: no gradients, glows or tints.

regions.label: route strip G → P → L → M
timetable: kind · name · value · line · file

options.label: Tracing-Paper Overlays
options.thesis: Config as stacked drafting sheets: each layer is a translucent sheet, and what Claude sees is the composite.
options.viewport: Same shell; the main pane shows the composite, and a layer slider peels sheets away to show what each file contributes.
options.risk: Translucent layering fights density and can turn into a costume on a working screen.

options.label: High-Density Modules
options.thesis: Dozens of small ruled modules, each a config source with a coloured tab, packed with no wasted pixel.
options.viewport: A mosaic of modules for the current repo (instructions, settings, hooks, MCP, agents, skills, memory), each with a tab and dense rows.
options.case: Holds product clarity on density, which you asked for; loses on showing load order, since modules have no sequence.
options.risk: Without a load-order spine, 'what wins' becomes guesswork.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: Pure black and white monospace data field.
options.viewport: Config as columns of monospace data.
options.risk: No colour means no way to show which scope a value comes from.
options.case: Loses on clarity: scope colour is the product.
options.kept: Tabular monospace alignment for every key, path and count.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: A visible construction grid as the armature.
options.viewport: Config laid on a visible cell grid.
options.risk: Monumental type wastes the density you need.
options.case: Loses both axes for a working screen.
options.kept: Whole-row grid: equal row heights, reflow by whole rows.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: The same subject registered across fixed plates.
options.viewport: Each layer as a plate on one baseline.
options.risk: Cream-and-serif is a stock AI look and far from developer culture.
options.kept: Registered side-by-side comparison of the same setting across layers.

options.label: Convention Catalog
options.thesis: A packed numbered grid keyed to a hall map.
options.viewport: Projects as stamp-sized cells keyed to a map.
options.risk: Thumbnails have nothing to show for text config.
options.kept: Map and list are one space, deep-linked both ways.

options.label: Guide Map Lobes
options.thesis: Flat colour lobes divided by coastline.
options.risk: Playful morphing fights a dense working tool.
options.kept: Flat, unmodulated colour with total commitment.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A developer dashboard done well: sidebar, cards, one accent colour.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar of projects, stat cards on top, tabs for instructions, settings and memory.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every dev dashboard, which you said would feel wrong.
